artifacts.summary: Re-research with live evidence: OAuth2 root cause is obsolete; himalaya now uses a valid Gmail app password (live SMTP AUTH returns 235 Accepted); config is home-manager managed from ~/.dotfiles/config/himalaya-config.toml; task's defect no longer reproduces.

next_steps: Verify one end-to-end send via <leader>me (expected to succeed), then close task 78 as resolved by the Feb-13 app-password migration; optionally create a cleanup task for dead OAuth2 remnants (legacy keyring entries, refresh-gmail-oauth2 script, plugin oauth defaults).

memory_candidates.content: In this environment, ~/.config/himalaya/config.toml (and other ~/.config files) are home-manager symlinks into the nix store; source of truth is ~/.dotfiles/config/ wired via modules/home/core/dotfiles.nix. Config changes require editing the dotfiles source + home-manager switch, while keyring secrets (secret-tool) are imperative and rotate without any rebuild.

Gmail SMTP auth for himalaya/mbsync uses a consumer-account app password stored in the keyring (service gmail-app-password); OAuth2/XOAUTH2 was abandoned 2026-07-02 (task 72) because Testing-mode refresh tokens expire in 7 days and Production verification of the restricted mail.google.com scope requires a paid CASA Tier 2 audit. A live AUTH PLAIN probe via openssl s_client to smtp.gmail.com:465 is a safe read-only way to verify SMTP credentials without sending mail.
